definitions: A model of open access publishing where the final published version of an article is immediately and permanently available online for free to everyone, typically with the author or their institution paying an article processing charge (APC).
A specific type of open access where scholarly articles are made freely available online by the publisher, often funded by author-side fees rather than subscriptions.
examples: Many researchers choose Gold Open Access for their publications.
The university has a fund to support Gold Open Access fees.
Publishing via Gold Open Access increases visibility.
